digest.component_or_area: Configuration ownership and credential boundary enforcement gate
propositions: An AST gate must detect and prohibit six categories of configuration/credential reads (ambient env, helper-shim env, load_config calls, literal getattr on os.environ, provider-credential reads, and backend-registry access) in modules below approved seams without duplication of gen_env_registry machinery.
The gate must resolve callee and receiver aliases (import, local variable binding) to detect evasions like `src = os.environ; src.get('SECRET')` and local-aliased load_config calls.

Owner sets and credential/adapter/env-baseline registries must be derived at runtime from existing sources (_child_env, decorator scans, gen_env_registry output) rather than hand-copied, with new unowned names and credential spellings causing gate failure.
Legacy-exception entries must be exact `path+symbol+rationale` tuples with no glob metacharacters, and self-tests must reject globs, missing rationales, and new unowned names.
The gate must exit 0 on the current codebase (covered by legacy exceptions) and 1 when a violation is detected, running entirely offline with no network dependency.
Synthetic fixtures for each of the six categories in both direct and aliased forms must demonstrate the expected failure diagnostics (path, symbol, access kind, owning seam).
